title: Adic surjectivity from the principal generators
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $r\geq0$ be an integer and let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$. Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $\widehat A_I=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$, with quotient transition maps and canonical map $c_I:A\to\widehat A_I$, $a\mapsto(a\bmod I^n)_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For each $i$ put $\widehat A_{(f_i)}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/f_i^nA$ and $c_i(a)=(a\bmod f_i^nA)_n$. If every $c_i:A\to\widehat A_{(f_i)}$ is surjective, then $c_I$ is surjective. No separatedness, Noetherianity or completeness of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 090S (lemma-when-surjective-to-completion), statement and proof, lines 22755–22773; specialization M=A.

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $I=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], the completion is the inverse limit of the constant system $A/0=A$ with identity maps, indexed by $n\geq1$. Every compatible family is constant and is the image of its first coordinate, so $c_I$ is surjective. Henceforth suppose $r\geq1$.

For $n\geq1$ put $J_n=(f_1^n,\ldots,f_r^n)$. Then $J_n\subseteq I^n$ and $I^{rn}\subseteq J_n$: expand a product of $rn$ elements of $I$ into a finite sum of multiples of products of $rn$ generators. In each such product some $f_i$ occurs at least $n$ times, since otherwise the total number of factors would be at most $r(n-1)<rn$. Each summand is therefore a multiple of some $f_i^n$. This argument uses only finite distributivity and the definition of ideal multiplication.

Let $\xi=(\xi_m)_{m\geq1}\in\widehat A_I$, viewed as compatible residue classes by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For each $n\geq1$ choose $a_n\in A$ representing $\xi_{rn}\in A/I^{rn}$. Compatibility gives $a_{n+1}-a_n\in I^{rn}\subseteq J_n$. Since $J_n$ is generated by the $f_i^n$, choose $x_{n,i}\in A$ such that $a_{n+1}-a_n=\sum_{i=1}^r f_i^n x_{n,i}$. Thus for every $N\geq1$ finite telescoping gives $a_N=a_1+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^r f_i^n x_{n,i}$.

For each $i$ and $N\geq1$ set $s_{i,N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}f_i^n x_{n,i}\in A$. For $M\geq N$, $s_{i,M}-s_{i,N}=\sum_{n=N}^{M-1}f_i^n x_{n,i}\in f_i^N A$. Therefore $(s_{i,N}\bmod f_i^N A)_{N\geq1}$ is a compatible family in $\widehat A_{(f_i)}$ by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The assumed surjectivity of $c_i$ gives $b_i\in A$ satisfying $b_i-s_{i,N}\in f_i^N A$ for every $N\geq1$. This defines the symbolic principal sums from the source without assuming that a series converges in $A$.

Put $a=a_1+\sum_{i=1}^r b_i$. For every $N\geq1$, the telescoping identity and the interchange of two finite sums give $a-a_N=\sum_{i=1}^r(b_i-s_{i,N})\in J_N\subseteq I^N$. Since $rN\geq N$, compatibility of $\xi$ says that the representative $a_N$ of $\xi_{rN}$ also represents $\xi_N$ modulo $I^N$. Hence $a\bmod I^N=\xi_N$ for every $N$. Equality of compatible sequences in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] yields $c_I(a)=\xi$, proving surjectivity. No uniqueness of the $b_i$, cancellation of a generator, or separatedness is used.

lean.note: Fin r enumerates the given r generators, including the empty family. The underlying function of AdicCompletion.of is the canonical completion map.
